title: Legacy model-weight retirement orchestration and migration pathways
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define and ship an orchestrated end-to-end retirement workflow for legacy model weights that minimizes customer disruption, automates pin propagation, and publishes actionable migration guidance and performance profiles. This ticket covers policy, customer notices, console/SDK/tooling changes, migration helpers, and a rollback/runbook.

Why now: We have a growing backlog of older model checkpoints that increase maintenance surface, complicate kernel selection, and add cost to storage and testing. Several small customers still pin to older variants; without an automated, empathetic retirement flow we risk surprise breakage and support load.

Scope:
- Policy and criteria for marking a model version as candidate for retirement (usage thresholds, security/bug fixes, performance regression, end-of-support by model upstream).
- Notice cadence and copy: 90/60/30/7 day notices + final sunset notice with exact timestamp and suggested replacements.
- Console banners, tenant-level notice center, and per-token API deprecation header (X-Model-Sunset or similar) to warn clients at request time.
- SDK and CLI warnings: deprecation logs, opt-in auto-migrate flag, and a pin-export manifest that surfaces where customers have pinned legacy versions.
- Migration assistant: UI flow + CLI tool that suggests target replacements based on published performance profiles and token-cost delta.
- Bulk migration API for Dedicated/Private customers to update pinning across projects/environments with validation and dry-run.
- Automated email/SMS cadence for high-usage customers and in-console modal for active sessions.
- Rollback plan and fallback model routing policy for first 72 hours after sunset.
- Internal dashboards to track migration progress, API error spikes, and support ticket volume.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: automatic model weight deletion from storage (handled by infra retention policy); upstream model licensing negotiations.

Success looks like: clear public timeline for retiring candidate versions, >=80% of affected customers migrated to recommended replacements before sunset, <2% increase in error rate attributable to retirements, and no high-severity P0 support incidents caused by the automation rollout.

risks_mitigations: Risk: customers who rely on internal fine-tuning artifacts break when upstream weights are retired. Mitigation: surface all pinned models and give clear mapping; offer 1:1 migration support for customers with private artifacts.
Risk: automated bulk migrations produce subtle behavior differences. Mitigation: require dry-run + sample validation traffic and a rollback snapshot before commit.
Risk: increased support load during migration window. Mitigation: CS to prepare canned responses and create priority routing for migration-related tickets.

Risk: Dedicated/Private customers have internal governance that prevents quick pin changes. Mitigation: provide Offline migration packages and step-by-step runbooks for on-prem teams; schedule coordinated maintenance windows.
Risk: metrics and dashboards not available in first rollout. Mitigation: gate sunset for more than 10 customers until per-model telemetry is live.
metrics: % of pinned routes migrated prior to sunset (target >= 80%)
Number of migration-related support tickets in a 14-day window around sunset (target < 2x baseline)
API error rate delta for affected models during 72-hour fallback (target < 2% absolute increase)
Average latency and token-cost delta between deprecated and replacement models (for reporting)
# of Dedicated/Private customers using bulk-migrate vs manual migration
